questions.questionText: If $\tan\alpha = \frac{m}{m+1}$ and $\tan\beta = \frac{1}{2m+1}$, then $\alpha + \beta$ is equal to:

explanation.summary: $\tan(\alpha+\beta) = \frac{\frac{m}{m+1} + \frac{1}{2m+1}}{1 - \frac{m}{(m+1)(2m+1)}} = \frac{2m^2+m+m+1}{2m^2+3m+1-m} = \frac{2m^2+2m+1}{2m^2+2m+1} = 1 \implies \alpha + \beta = \pi/4$.

stepByStep.title: Official Solution
stepByStep.content: $\tan(\alpha+\beta) = \frac{\frac{m}{m+1} + \frac{1}{2m+1}}{1 - \frac{m}{(m+1)(2m+1)}} = \frac{2m^2+m+m+1}{2m^2+3m+1-m} = \frac{2m^2+2m+1}{2m^2+2m+1} = 1 \implies \alpha + \beta = \pi/4$.

explanation.summary: $dy/dx = \frac{4}{2\sqrt{4x-3}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{4x-3}} = 2/3 \implies \sqrt{4x-3} = 3 \implies 4x-3 = 9 \implies x = 3$. At $x=3$, $y = \sqrt{9}-1 = 2$. Point is $(3, 2)$.

questions.questionText: If $x = a\cos t, y = b\sin t$, then $\frac{d^2 y}{dx^2}$ is:

explanation.summary: $dx/dt = -a\sin t, dy/dt = b\cos t \implies dy/dx = -\frac{b}{a}\cot t$. $\frac{d^2 y}{dx^2} = \frac{b}{a}\csc^2 t \frac{dt}{dx} = -\frac{b}{a^2}\csc^3 t = -\frac{b}{a^2 (y/b)^3} = -\frac{b^4}{a^2 y^3}$.

stepByStep.title: Official Solution
stepByStep.content: $dx/dt = -a\sin t, dy/dt = b\cos t \implies dy/dx = -\frac{b}{a}\cot t$. $\frac{d^2 y}{dx^2} = \frac{b}{a}\csc^2 t \frac{dt}{dx} = -\frac{b}{a^2}\csc^3 t = -\frac{b}{a^2 (y/b)^3} = -\frac{b^4}{a^2 y^3}$.

By Cayley-Hamilton theorem, $A^3 - 6A^2 + 11A - 6I = 0 \implies 6A^{-1} = A^2 - 6A + 11I$. Thus $c = -6, d = 11$.

With $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=3$ and $|\vec{a}|^2=2$, $\vec{b} = -\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$ (or tests match (a)).

explanation.summary: $P(\text{odd}) = 3/4, P(\text{even}) = 1/4$. Sum is even if both are odd or both are even: $(3/4)^2 + (1/4)^2 = 9/16 + 1/16 = 10/16 = 5/8$.

questions.questionText: A man observes angle of elevation of top of mountain to be $30^\circ$. Walking 1000 ft nearer, angle is $45^\circ$. What is the distance of first observation point from foot of mountain?

explanation.summary: Let height be $h$. $d_2 = h\cot 45^\circ = h$, $d_1 = h\cot 30^\circ = h\sqrt{3}$. $d_1 - d_2 = h(\sqrt{3}-1) = 1000 \implies h = \frac{1000}{\sqrt{3}-1} = 500(\sqrt{3}+1)$. First point distance $d_1 = h\sqrt{3} = 500\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}+1)\text{ ft}$.

stepByStep.title: Official Solution
stepByStep.content: Let height be $h$. $d_2 = h\cot 45^\circ = h$, $d_1 = h\cot 30^\circ = h\sqrt{3}$. $d_1 - d_2 = h(\sqrt{3}-1) = 1000 \implies h = \frac{1000}{\sqrt{3}-1} = 500(\sqrt{3}+1)$. First point distance $d_1 = h\sqrt{3} = 500\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}+1)\text{ ft}$.

explanation.summary: Vowels: O, O, A, I, O (5 vowels: 3 O's, 1 A, 1 I). Consonants: C, R, P, R, T, N (6 consonants: 2 R's). Treat vowels as single block: 7 units arranged in $\frac{7!}{2!} = 2520$ ways. Vowels arranged inside block in $\frac{5!}{3!} = 20$ ways. Total = $2520 \times 20 = 50400$.

stepByStep.title: Official Solution
stepByStep.content: Vowels: O, O, A, I, O (5 vowels: 3 O's, 1 A, 1 I). Consonants: C, R, P, R, T, N (6 consonants: 2 R's). Treat vowels as single block: 7 units arranged in $\frac{7!}{2!} = 2520$ ways. Vowels arranged inside block in $\frac{5!}{3!} = 20$ ways. Total = $2520 \times 20 = 50400$.

stepByStep.title: Official Solution
stepByStep.content: $(a+b)^2 - c^2 = ab \implies a^2 + b^2 - c^2 = -ab \implies \frac{a^2+b^2-c^2}{2ab} = -1/2 \implies \cos C = -1/2 \implies C = 2\pi/3$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: If $f(x) = \tan^{-1}\left[\frac{\sin x}{1 + \cos x}\right]$, then what is the first derivative of $f(x)$?

explanation.summary: $\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos x} = \frac{2\sin(x/2)\cos(x/2)}{2\cos^2(x/2)} = \tan(x/2)$. Thus $f(x) = x/2 \implies f'(x) = 1/2$.

stepByStep.title: Official Solution
stepByStep.content: $\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos x} = \frac{2\sin(x/2)\cos(x/2)}{2\cos^2(x/2)} = \tan(x/2)$. Thus $f(x) = x/2 \implies f'(x) = 1/2$.

explanation.summary: $\binom{n+1}{3} - \binom{n}{3} = \binom{n}{2} = \frac{n(n-1)}{2} = 21 \implies n(n-1) = 42 \implies n = 7$.

stepByStep.title: Official Solution
stepByStep.content: $\binom{n+1}{3} - \binom{n}{3} = \binom{n}{2} = \frac{n(n-1)}{2} = 21 \implies n(n-1) = 42 \implies n = 7$.
